newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan ends first day of testimony to Congress.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan ends first day of testimony to Congress.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan ended the first leg of his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress on Tuesday.

In a formal statement to a House Banking subcommittee, Greenspan said the Federal Reserve must be ready to act if necessary to head off inflation, but that growth seems to be slowing for the time being.

Greenspan will address the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday at 1000 a.m. EDT (1400 GMT), in the second leg of the Fed's semiannual statement on the economy. He will repeat his formal remarks and then answer questions from Senators.
Also at 10 a.m. on Wednesday, Fed Vice Chairwoman Alice Rivlin, Fed Governor Laurence Meyer and New York Fed President William McDonough will testify to the House Banking Committee.
